caption: "lizzie borden" — 500,000+ searches this week. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about the woman behind Netflix's new Monster.
Why: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story landed on Netflix on September 17, all eight episodes at once, with Ella Beatty as Lizzie. It is the fourth season of the anthology and the first about a woman.

What most people don't know: Lizzie Borden was acquitted. Her father and stepmother were killed with a hatchet in Fall River on August 4, 1892. A New Bedford jury took under two hours to find her not guilty. The rhyme is wrong: about 19 blows and 11, not 40 and 41.
Very simply put: America's most famous axe murderer was never convicted.

slides.headline: The woman in Netflix's new Monster was found *not guilty*.
slides.sub: 10 things most people don't know about Lizzie Borden, 500,000+ searches this week.

slides.headline: Two killed with a hatchet on *August 4, 1892*.
slides.sub: Andrew Borden and his wife Abby, at home on Second Street in Fall River, Massachusetts.
slides.image: A Victorian wooden staircase and hallway with morning light through a lace curtain, staircase in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark wooden floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: The rhyme says 40 whacks. The count was about *19*.
slides.sub: Abby was struck 18 or 19 times, Andrew 10 or 11, according to the autopsies.
slides.image: An open antique ledger with a fountain pen on a dark oak desk under a brass lamp, ledger in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark wood, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: The jury took *under two hours*.
slides.sub: Trial in New Bedford, June 5 to 20, 1893. Verdict: not guilty.
slides.image: An empty 19th-century courtroom with a wooden jury box and tall windows, jury box in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain wooden floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: The day before, she reportedly asked for *prussic acid*.
slides.sub: A pharmacist said she wanted the poison to clean a sealskin cloak. The court excluded his testimony.
slides.image: Antique brown glass apothecary bottles on a wooden pharmacy shelf in warm light, bottles in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain wooden counter, photorealistic, no readable labels, no text

slides.headline: Her father was a bank president with *no indoor plumbing*.
slides.sub: Andrew Borden refused plumbing and electricity. A two-stall privy in the basement, a chamber pot under every bed.
slides.image: A white enamel chamber pot beside an iron bed in a bare Victorian bedroom, bed in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain floorboards, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: She changed her name to *Lizbeth* and bought a mansion.
slides.sub: Maplecroft, on The Hill in Fall River. Her sister Emma moved out in 1905 after a party for an actress.
slides.image: A grand Victorian mansion with a wide porch behind maple trees in autumn sunlight, house in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain lawn, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: She left *$30,000* to an animal rescue league.
slides.sub: She died June 1, 1927, aged 66, worth over $250,000. Emma died nine days later.
slides.image: A small dog and a cat sitting together on a stone step in soft daylight, animals in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain stone, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: The murder house is a *bed and breakfast*.
slides.sub: 230 Second Street, a B&B since 1996, sold for $2 million in 2021. Abby's room is the most requested.
slides.image: A neatly made antique bed with a white quilt in a sunlit Victorian guest room, bed in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain floral carpet, photorealistic, no people, no text
